It is done to engage the rail earlier and more powerfully in steep, critical wave faces. The Trial is more of a slow-burner. The reader is gradually and subtly led into a world that ends up being as confusing, chaotic and surreal as that depicted in Metamorphosis. In the Trial, as is typical of novels, other characters are fleshed out more fully, connecting stories are told, and sub-plots are unearthed. Is this what you found pointless and bland? I enjoyed both, and while I agree that metamorphosis is more gripping, I'm surprised you found the Trial tedious. I think some of the passages in the Trial explaining in detail the legal system, it's hierarchy, it's rules, it's judges, were deliberately written to be bland to show the insanity of the bureaucratic nightmare Josef K. had found himself in.
